body.text:
大家好！我是美国人，在上海学中文已经一年了。上个周末我和朋友去杭州玩，我们在西湖旁边走路了三个小时，风景非常好看。

但是我有一个问题：我在一个饭馆点了西湖醋鱼，服务员说这个菜很有名，可是我觉得它太酸了，我不是很喜欢吃。是不是我点得不对？还有什么杭州菜你们推荐我试一试吗？谢谢！
body.background: A post on Xiaohongshu after my weekend in Hangzhou.

out.title: 回复在杭州问西湖醋鱼的美国朋友
out.audience: Chinese travel-lovers and locals who follow food and travel notes
out.purpose: Share a Hangzhou weekend and ask which dishes to try

parts.problem: A Chinese travel writer would show the scenery through its effect on the visitor, for example that it made them unwilling to leave. 风景非常好看 is a complete judgment with nothing behind it, so the praise is thin and the reader has nothing to picture.

parts.problem: Here 有一个问题 announces a real difficulty, and Chinese readers expect the writer to say what went wrong, such as bad service, a bad dish or a bad experience. The post then asks only whether the writer ordered the wrong thing, so the frame promises more than the question delivers.

out.construct: 风景好到让人⟨…⟩ — the scenery is so good that it makes people …

why.label: 西湖
why.note: Keep the name as the writer gives it. Note that the post says West Lake, so readers will know exactly which place is meant.

why.label: 沿着
why.note: Here 沿着 pictures the walking route along the lake. The writer's 在…旁边走路 only places them beside it, which is flatter. Example: 沿着西湖走 (walk along West Lake).

why.label: 好到
why.note: 好到 makes the praise the result of the view, so the reader sees how good it was. Writing 风景很好看 alone only states a judgment, which is the problem with the draft.

why.label: 舍不得
why.note: 舍不得 (reluctant to leave) shows the effect on the visitor, the typical way Chinese travel posts show scenery. A plain 很美 gives the reader nothing to picture.

why.label: 挪不开眼
why.note: 挪不开眼 (cannot take eyes off) is a common image for a view that holds you, a stronger picture than repeating 好看. It works well as the second beat after the 舍不得 line.

out.prompt: Rewrite this opening so the scenery lands on the reader instead of being just a label.
out.success: 哈哈舍不得走才是真的好看！我也想去了～

out.construct: 对我来说+形容词 (for me, it's too …)

why.label: 对我来说
why.note: Makes the verdict about your own taste. Without it, '太酸了' reads as 'the dish is too sour', which insults a famous Hangzhou dish. With it, you're saying the dish is not for you.

why.label: 点错了
why.note: The everyday way to say 'I ordered wrong'. '点得不对' is a literal, slightly stiff phrasing that sounds like a translation from English.

why.label: 下次去杭州
why.note: Gives the recommendation request its reason. Readers need to know you're planning a future visit, not asking for a menu right now. It sits before the question so the 'next time' idea is clear.

why.label: 我不太喜欢吃
why.note: 不太 is the everyday hedge in speech. 不是很 is grammatical but stiffer and easy to misread as a flat, emphatic dislike.

out.prompt: Rewrite this part of your post so it's clear what the problem was and what you want to know next.
out.success: 哦，原来是口味不合呀，那我给你推荐几道！

out.plan: Announce the problem first, then describe what happened, and use a contrast clause to shift to your own taste. Then ask a direct yes-or-no question about your choice and end with a request tied to your next visit, so the question and the request carry the most weight.
out.example: [但是我有一个问题]：我在超市买了一包咖啡豆，店员说这个牌子很好，[可是对我来说]太苦了，我不太喜欢喝。[是不是我]选错了？

out.gloss: A noun meaning someone's taste preference in flavor, such as liking light or strong food. It goes with adjectives like 清淡, 重, or 偏甜, and with 合...口味 (to suit one's taste). It is neutral in register.
out.example: 他的口味比较清淡，平时很少吃辣。

out.gloss: An adjective meaning suitable, fitting, or appropriate for a purpose, size, or situation. It is often used as 合适 + noun, or 不合适 for something that doesn't fit or isn't appropriate. It is neutral in register.
out.example: 这双鞋大小正合适，我就买下来了。

out.gloss: A verb-complement compound meaning to order the wrong thing by mistake, with 错 showing the mistake. It is usually followed by 了 (点错了) and used for ordering food, drinks, or items online.
out.example: 他在网上买东西时点错了尺码，只好退货。

out.gloss: A time expression meaning next time, referring to a future occasion of the same kind. It is used alone or before a verb phrase, such as 下次再来 or 下次注意, and is neutral in register.
out.example: 今天的球赛太精彩了，下次我们还一起来看。

out.gloss: A verb meaning to recommend something or someone to another person. The usual pattern is 推荐 + thing + 给 + person, or 推荐 + noun, and it is neutral in register.
out.example: 这本小说是我姐姐推荐给我的，我看得停不下来。

out.gloss: A verb meaning to like, followed by a noun or a verb phrase. 不太喜欢 is a softer, more polite way to say you don't really like something, and it is neutral in register.
out.example: 我妹妹很喜欢养猫，家里现在有两只。

out.plan: Announce the problem first, then describe what happened, and use a contrast clause to shift to your own taste. Then ask a direct yes-or-no question about your choice and end with a request tied to your next visit, so the question and the request carry the most weight.

issues.note: "你指的" points to nothing earlier in the post, so this clause reads as a fragment joined onto the sentence before it.
